gen_text: Each product holds a name, a description, a price and an image.
Given a product that is referred to by order items of an order, When that order is removed, Then the product continues to exist.

Given a known customer, one or more order items each referring to an existing product, and a payment method, When the customer submits the order, Then the system registers an order with the submission date as its order date and the status submitted.
Given an order submission that names a customer not known to the system, When the submission is made, Then the system rejects it and registers no order.
Given an order submission that contains no order item, When the submission is made, Then the system rejects it and registers no order.
A newly registered order has the status submitted, from which its status may change only to pending.

Given an order whose status is filled or shipped and that has no invoice, When the accountant raises an invoice for it with a date, an amount and a payment method, Then the system records the invoice for that order with the status issued.
Given an order that already has an invoice, When the accountant requests a further invoice for it, Then the system rejects the request and the order keeps its single invoice.
Given an order whose status is submitted, pending or closed, When the accountant requests an invoice for it, Then the system rejects the request and records no invoice.
Each invoice records a date, an amount, a status and a payment method, none of which may be absent.
The amount of an invoice is a decimal number.

Given an invoice whose status is issued, When the customer submits a payment against it with a date, an amount and a payment method, Then the system records the payment against that invoice with the status pending.
Given an invoice whose status is paid, When the customer submits a payment against it, Then the system rejects the payment and records no payment.
Each payment records a date, an amount, a status and a payment method, none of which may be absent.
An invoice may have any number of payments, and each payment is recorded against exactly one invoice and never directly against an order.
Given an order whose status is submitted, When order staff receive it, Then the system sets its status to pending.
Given an order whose status is not submitted, When order staff attempt to receive it, Then the system rejects the attempt and the status of the order is unchanged.
Given an order whose status is pending, When order staff mark it as filled, Then the system sets its status to filled.
Given an order whose status is not pending, When order staff attempt to mark it as filled, Then the system rejects the attempt and the status of the order is unchanged.
Given an order whose status is not pending, When order staff attempt to decline it, Then the system rejects the attempt and the status of the order is unchanged.
Given an order whose status is not filled, When order staff attempt to set it to shipped, Then the system rejects the attempt and the status of the order is unchanged.
Given an order that has an invoice with payments against it, When order staff set the order to shipped, Then the status of the invoice and the status of every payment against it are unchanged.
Given an order whose status is filled and that has no invoice, When order staff set it to shipped, Then the system sets its status to shipped without requiring an invoice to have been raised.
Given a payment whose status is pending, When the accountant confirms it, Then the system sets its status to completed.
Given a pending payment against an invoice whose status is issued, When the accountant confirms the payment, Then the system sets the status of that invoice to paid.
Given a payment whose status is not pending, When the accountant attempts to confirm it, Then the system rejects the attempt and the status of the payment is unchanged.
Confirming a payment changes the status of the payment only from pending to completed and the status of its invoice only from issued to paid.
Given a payment whose status is pending, When the accountant rejects it, Then the system sets its status to failed.
Rejecting a payment changes its status only from pending to failed.
Once an order has the status closed, its status never changes again.
Given an order submission in which an order item refers to a product that does not exist, When the submission is made, Then the system rejects it and registers no order.
Each order records an order date, a total amount, a status and a payment method, none of which may be absent.
The payment method of an invoice takes only the values bank, card or cash.

Given an invoice whose earlier payment has the status failed, When the customer submits a further payment against it, Then the system records the further payment as a separate payment with the status pending and the earlier payment keeps the status failed.
A newly submitted payment has the status pending, from which its status may change only to completed or to failed.
Receiving an order changes its status only from submitted to pending.
Marking an order as filled changes its status only from pending to filled.
Given an order whose status is closed, When order staff attempt to decline it, Then the system rejects the attempt and the order keeps the status closed.
Given a pending payment against an invoice that bills an order, When the accountant rejects the payment, Then the status of the invoice and the status of the order are unchanged.
Given an order whose invoice has the status paid and whose status is not shipped, When order staff attempt to close it, Then the system rejects the attempt and the status of the order is unchanged.
Closing an order changes its status only from shipped to closed.
